ranges: SPDX/imports connect Arc, Arrow arrays/batches, Bytes/BufMut, core Schema/Result, compression parameters, BatchEncoder/EncodedBatch, object store/writer/path, Tokio async writes, generated metadata/MAGIC and shared sink/pipeline/body functions. super::encoding_strategy supplies exact version composition.

Public Writer owns private StructuralFileSink, EncodingPipeline and CompressionParams. It has no Clone/Debug derive or local Drop implementation. Documentation assigns exact V2_1 composition, finish order and footer identity to this wrapper; shared components do not choose its version.

try_new delegates explicit-schema construction with default CompressionParams. try_new_with_compression first creates a lazy writer, then initializes it and returns Result. Initialization failure drops that temporary owned writer; no explicit async abort/cleanup is awaited here.

new_lazy supplies default compression. new_lazy_with_compression constructs a sink from the owned object writer and a pipeline from options, storing compression unchanged. It is infallible and does not validate options/schema, create encoders or perform IO.

Private initialize orders option validation, encoding_options computation, schema.validate, exact strategy creation from cloned compression, BatchEncoder::try_new, then pipeline initialization. A supplied cache budget with an empty schema can divide by zero during option computation before schema validation (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:414-419). ensure_initialized converts the first RecordBatch Arrow schema only when schema is absent, then calls initialize; an empty batch can still initialize.

Consuming with_page_metadata_spill sets sink Pending and returns self; it adds no timing/state guard. write_batches awaits write_batch for each borrowed batch in iterator order and stops on first error; an empty iterator performs no initialization or IO.

write_batch ensures initialization, then delegates to pipeline. write_column delegates directly, without lazy schema inference; it requires an existing schema and uses a top-level field index, not a physical column index. It advances only that field through the shared pipeline and can create unequal field lengths.

write_external_buffer directly delegates to the sink alignment/write method and returns position/length. add_schema_metadata delegates insertion into the pipeline map. Neither requires schema initialization or validates that later external metadata actually refers to written bytes.

initialize_with_external_metadata returns unit: update pipeline schema/declared row count, then replace sink metadata. It does not validate schema/options/grammar, recreate/reset existing encoders or rebuild field mapping. add_global_buffer immediately writes via sink and returns one-based user-buffer index; descriptor later occupies table index0.

finish for V2_1 awaits pipeline flush then finish_encoders, constructs descriptor, writes descriptor/global table entries, obtains column-metadata start, writes all column metadata, then column offset table followed by global offset table. num_global_buffers is unchecked len as u32; sink supplies its declared column count. Failures propagate at each step with no local rollback/finished flag. Even a never-initialized lazy writer first flushes the sink before descriptor creation rejects unknown schema.

Footer fields in order: u64 LE column_metadata_start, column_metadata_offsets_start, global_buffer_offsets_start; u32 LE global-buffer count and column count; u16 LE major2 and minor1; four-byte MAGIC LANC. Total40 bytes (rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:33-33). Return pipeline rows_written with size from awaited object shutdown. No checksum, terminator retry guard, uniform field-length validation or explicit footer alignment is added. A partial footer or shutdown error does not restore consumed encoders/metadata.

Public async abort(&mut self) has an empty body and does not drop, replace, shutdown or abort the owned sink. Its comment refers to dropping a multipart ObjectWriter, which this call does not do. tell delegates current object position, not durable size. field_id_to_column_indices borrows pipeline mapping unchanged. No local state machine prevents writes/finish calls afterward.

concat_lance_footer borrows EncodedBatch, calls shared encode_batch_body(batch,write_schema), appends the same40-byte footer with literal(2,1), then freezes BytesMut. It performs no IO or exact-version grammar validation; it assumes supplied batch data/metadata fit this version. Shared body conversion retains given descriptors and optional schema; parent chooses self-described versus mini mode.

files.role: Crate-internal structural writer mechanisms shared by exact V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 wrappers. Public declarations here are effectively crate-visible through writer::structural. StructuralFileSink owns object IO, metadata/spill and offset tables; EncodingPipeline owns schema, field encoders, runtime options and row accounting. Private spill/descriptor/nullability helpers and four local tests complete the file.
files.limits: All 1,025 physical lines read in ANALYZE55. Explicit source operations and deductions about ordering, padding and partial mutation are documented; no runtime failure or performance measurement is claimed. Underlying FieldEncoder/RepDef/compression algorithms and ObjectWriter backend durability/Drop/flush remain pending. There is no explicit unsafe block, local task spawn, synchronization lock or cleanup-on-drop implementation in this file. Test source was read, not executed.
ranges: SPDX/imports include panic macro, HashMap/Arc, Arrow array/struct reconstruction, BooleanBuffer, Bytes cursors/mutation, FuturesOrdered, core schema/errors/padding, encoding pages/tasks/options/out-of-line buffers and RepDefBuilder, ObjectStore/Writer, logs, path, prost Message/Any, Tokio AsyncWrite and tracing. Local file adapters supply schema protobuf and runtime constants.

PAD_BUFFER is64 bytes each decimal72 (0x48), using PAGE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT. MAX_PAGE_BYTES is32MiB; comment calls it best-effort memory bound because V2.1+ splits reads. DEFAULT_SPILL_BUFFER_LIMIT is256KiB serialized page metadata, not a global heap cap. Alignment declaration is rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:24-24.

Private PageMetadataSpill owns sidecar writer/store/path, logical position, per-column serialized byte Vecs and chunk descriptor Vecs, plus threshold. Async new creates sidecar first, then threshold=max(256KiB/max(num_columns,1),64) and empty vectors of num_columns. Many columns can exceed the nominal aggregate budget due to64 minimum, retained capacities and chunk descriptors; no column count validation or sidecar exclusivity check is local.

append_page directly indexes the column buffer, protobuf length-delimited encodes one Page, wraps encoding failures as IO with std::io InvalidData, and flushes once buffer length reaches/exceeds threshold. It can overshoot by one whole page; index is trusted and panic-capable. No page sort or deduplication.

flush_column returns immediately if empty; otherwise write_all current bytes, then record(position,len as u32), advance position by len as u64 and clear the Vec without releasing capacity. Casts/addition are unchecked. Failed/partial writes leave the buffer and recorded position unchanged, so retry is not guaranteed safe. shutdown_writer flushes columns sequentially, awaits ObjectWriter::shutdown, discards summary.

decode_spilled_chunk clones Bytes handle into a cursor, repeatedly decodes length-delimited Page until no bytes remain, collecting all decoded pages in Vec. Decode errors become IO/InvalidData; earlier pages are discarded on error. Empty bytes return empty pages. It checks protobuf syntax only, not page grammar or buffer addresses.

Private PageSpillState is Pending(store,path) or Active(PageMetadataSpill), with absence represented by outer Option. initial_column_metadata returns empty page/offset/size Vecs and encoding=None. No Drop cleanup, committed state or default page encoding here.

StructuralFileSink owns object writer, complete column metadata Vec, u32 declared column count, user global-buffer descriptors and optional spill state. new stores writer, zero count and empty state; no IO or validation. Documentation explicitly delegates exact grammar/composition/footer ordering to callers.

with_page_metadata_spill unconditionally replaces prior spill state with Pending. initialize_columns replaces column metadata with blank entries and updates count; initialize_with_external_metadata replaces metadata and unchecked-casts Vec length to u32. Neither resets global buffers/spill, migrates existing pages, checks state, or validates external encodings. Reconfiguring an active/populated sink can lose previously retained metadata.

write_aligned_buffer_to writes payload then pad_bytes<64>(payload.len) copies of0x48; it aligns length, not current starting position. write_aligned_buffer delegates through object writer, and write_raw writes only payload. Empty payload requires no pad. A misaligned current position is not repaired by post-padding; both write calls may fail after partial mutation.

write_page consumes EncodedPage data, records tell before each payload, stores unpadded length and writes with trailing alignment. After all payload bytes, prost Any-wrap Legacy or Structural description without restricting version/grammar. Construct Direct encoding Page with num_rows as length and row_number as priority, then unchecked-cast physical column index to usize. Serialization failure can follow already-written data.

On the first page after configuring Pending, take the pending state, asynchronously create a sidecar sized to current num_columns and install Active. Failure/cancellation during creation leaves page_spill None after data was written. Active appends page; None pushes into column_metadata[column_index]; unreachable branches enforce immediately checked private states. Bounds are trusted. Pages retained before spill activation are not copied into sidecar.

Debug-instrumented write_pages owns FuturesOrdered<EncodeTask>, polls ordered results and writes each successful page sequentially. An error drops remaining task futures and returns without the final flush; underlying spawned work is not established here. After all tasks (even none), await AsyncWriteExt::flush. Source comment says this reaps already-failed uploads without waiting for in-flight ones; actual backend poll_flush implementation remains pending, so flush is not asserted durable.

write_column_buffer_at writes a length-padded payload at current writer position, then records the caller-supplied position and original length under column index. It never seeks or checks supplied position against tell. set_column_encoding overwrites Some(encoding) in the indexed metadata. Both trust index; metadata may be mutated only after some bytes are already written.

add_global_buffer captures current position, writes payload with trailing0x48 padding, appends(position,unpadded length) and returns Vec length cast u32. This is a one-based user index because descriptor is inserted first later; no overflow or initial-position alignment check. Buffer may be empty.

write_global_buffers serializes descriptor and writes it raw at current position, then returns descriptor tuple first followed by draining all user-global tuples. User global payloads were already written earlier. Descriptor has no length prefix or trailing padding. Private write_column_metadata likewise writes raw protobuf bytes at current position and returns position/length; no CRC, outer prefix or alignment.

write_column_metadatas takes all column metadata and spill state out of self before awaits. Active spill flushes/shuts down its writer, opens sidecar for reading, and takes chunk vectors; Pending/None produce no reader. Failure loses these taken in-memory states from the sink and can leave a sidecar object. No retry/rollback guard or explicit sidecar deletion is implemented.

For each column in order, Active spill reads every recorded chunk sequentially via unchecked usize range arithmetic, decodes all pages and accumulates one complete column Vec. Replace metadata.pages with that Vec, discarding any pages retained before spill activation/external initialization. Serialize/write whole column, push position. Peak memory still includes full-column pages and serialized bytes plus chunk descriptors; spill does not stream one page into final metadata. No sidecar cleanup after success.

write_offset_table records start and writes every(position,len) as two LEu64 values, sixteen bytes per entry. Empty table emits nothing and returns current position. No count prefix, padding, overflow validation or bounds checks.

write_external_buffer computes leading zero padding from current position modulo64, writes that padding then payload raw, and returns aligned start plus unpadded length. This differs from ordinary trailing0x48 padding: its ending can be unaligned. Position cast to usize and additions are unchecked. A later ordinary aligned-buffer write assumes the caller has restored an aligned starting position.

output_mut exposes mutable dyn ObjectWriter to crate callers; tell casts backend position to u64. num_columns returns stored count even after metadata is drained. shutdown awaits ObjectWriter::shutdown and returns summary.size cast u64, discarding other summary fields. No local closed-state tracking or automatic abort.

EncodingPipeline privately stores optional schema/ExpectedTypes, owned field encoder Vec, mapping Vec, aggregate rows, per-field rows, schema metadata map and FileWriterOptions. new initializes empty/zero state without validating options. validate_options simply delegates FileWriterOptions::validate (only explicit max_page_bytes=Some(0) rejected at rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:56-65).

encoding_options divides supplied data_cache_bytes by top-level schema.fields.len, truncating remainder; empty schema with a supplied budget divides by zero. Otherwise use8MiB per top-level field. Explicit max_page_bytes wins; else read LANCE_FILE_WRITER_MAX_PAGE_BYTES and parse untrimmed u64, warning on parse failure then32MiB; missing/non-Unicode env also falls back without warning. Parsed0 is accepted because explicit-options validation occurred separately. No environment memoization.

EncodingOptions receives derived budgets, keep_original_array defaultfalse and alignment64. This differs from raw EncodingOptions::default keep_original_array=true (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:277-285). initialize sets sink physical column count, zeroes field-row vector, moves encoder Vec/mapping, merges drained schema metadata into existing map (schema keys win), then stores schema. It does not reset rows_written or cached expected_types; normal wrappers call it once.

is_initialized tests only schema presence, not encoders or sink state. verify_field_nullability starts recursive validation with every slot reachable. Comments explain null struct parents hide child nulls and dictionary logical nulls may exist without physical key nulls; external Arrow behavior is rationale, while the implementation below explicitly uses logical_nulls.

Recursive nullability computes logical_nulls; absent mask means0 offending, top-level uses null_count, otherwise count((NOT validity) AND reachable). A nonnullable field with visible nulls returns InvalidInput naming the field, not the count/path. Empty field.children ends recursion. Counts/masks assume array shape consistent with field.

For any non-StructArray with children, zip declared children with ArrayData.child_data, clone/reconstruct each child Array and recurse with reachable=None. Parent reachability is deliberately not propagated across list-like offsets. Zip ignores unmatched tails; this helper does not independently enforce child count/type. It checks all exposed child-data slots, not only referenced list positions.

For StructArray, own validity is logical mask or all-set BooleanBuffer of parent length. Child reachability is own AND inherited mask, or own at root. Zip schema children with parent.columns and recurse in order, stopping at first error. Sliced StructArray columns already align to parent window per source comment and local test. Child-count mismatch is not checked here.

verify_nullability_constraints zips batch.columns in supplied positional order with stored schema.fields and recursively checks each pair. It unwraps initialized schema. Unlike ExpectedTypes::check_batch and encode_batch, it does not match top-level names; reordered input can therefore be checked against a different field nullability. Extra/missing positional tails are ignored by zip; separate type/encoding stages own other validation.

encode_columns first copies each selected field current row number into a Vec, then iterates fields in order and calls that mutable encoder maybe_encode with cloned Arc array, shared out-of-line buffer planner, fresh default RepDefBuilder, old row number and array length. Direct indexing trusts field/encoder/count coherence. Collect Result<Vec<Vec<EncodeTask>>>; later failure does not roll back earlier encoder mutations or external-buffer reservations.

encode_batch builds field/index/ArrayRef pairs by stored schema order and batch.column_by_name. Missing field gives InvalidInput naming it before any maybe_encode call, because all lookups collect first. Extra batch columns are omitted here. The schema Option unwrap assumes initialization; ArrayRef cloning shares input data, and actual copy/retain policy is delegated to encoders.

Debug-instrumented write_batch logs dimensions/memory estimate, expects initialized schema, lazily builds ExpectedTypes and checks types, then positional nullability. Zero rows return only after these checks. Each individual batch above u32MAX rows is rejected, despite diagnostic phrasing about whole files; cumulative count uses u64 later. An empty batch can return before missing-name detection in encode_batch.

Start OutOfLineBuffers at sink tell/alignment64, synchronously build encoder tasks, write all reserved buffers with trailing padding, flatten tasks into FuturesOrdered. Only then checked_add aggregate u64 rows; overflow returns InvalidInput after encoder mutation and possible buffer IO. On success increment every field counter and aggregate before awaiting page writes. Page/flush failure leaves those counters advanced; no transactional retry guarantee. Per-field increments are unchecked arithmetic.

write_column requires schema presence or InvalidInput mentioning explicit schema (a previously initialized lazy writer also satisfies actual check). Get top-level field by index with contextual bounds error; reject this array length above u32MAX before type/nullability validation. No inference from a bare array.

Lazily build ExpectedTypes, check selected column type, then logical nullability; empty arrays return afterward. Encode singleton field with out-of-line planner, write reserved buffers, order tasks, then unchecked-add selected field count and set aggregate rows=max(old aggregate,new field total) before awaiting pages. Other fields unchanged and differing lengths permitted; no cumulative overflow check here. External-metadata initialization alone may leave encoder/count vectors empty and make a later nonempty column write panic on indexing.

flush obtains current tell, calls every field encoder flush sequentially into a fallible task Vec, writes returned out-of-line buffers with trailing padding and drains flattened ordered tasks via sink.write_pages. It does not advance row counters or finish encoders. With zero encoders it still asks position and flushes writer through empty task drain. Partial encoder/IO state is not restored after failure.

finish_encoders returns immediately if no encoders. Otherwise std::mem::take removes all encoders from self, then each writer.finish is awaited with a fresh OutOfLineBuffers planner. Returned external buffers are written raw, unlike batch/flush aligned writes. Planner advances virtual positions including padding but does not insert padding into buffer payloads (rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:130-159); correctness of multiple unaligned finish buffers therefore depends on producer invariants. Debug assertion compares emitted count to each encoder num_columns after IO.

For each finished column, write final pages then set buffer_position=tell once. Each column buffer is written with trailing padding but recorded position advances only by raw buffer.len; two unaligned buffers can produce recorded offsets different from actual later starts. No seek/check or padding adjustment here. Any-wrap column encoding into Direct, set metadata, increment physical column_index. Final pages carry their own column indices; they are not rewritten to this counter.

After all encoders, mismatching physical count panics with expected/actual even in release builds. Success does not validate row equality. add_schema_metadata replaces duplicate key. initialize_with_external_metadata drains/merges schema metadata, stores schema and rows_written only; existing encoders, expected-types cache, mapping and field counters remain unchanged. It returns unit and bypasses validation.

make_file_descriptor errors InvalidInput if schema absent. Otherwise move accumulated metadata back into schema, recursively unload blobs in place, and call private descriptor builder with aggregate rows. This mutates schema before later IO; repeated calls can replace metadata with empty drained map. rows_written getter returns aggregate; field_id_to_column_indices borrows mapping with no consistency check.

Private make_file_descriptor converts borrowed core Schema through FieldsWithMeta, builds Some(pb::Schema) and declared length, always Ok locally. No row reconciliation or schema validation. Public-in-crate EncodedBatchBody holds BytesMut plus threeu64 start offsets and two u32 counts for exact wrapper footer append; it carries no version.

encode_batch_body reserves batch.data.len+1MiB with unchecked addition, copies full data into BytesMut, optionally clones batch core Schema via TryFrom<&Self>, serializes descriptor and appends it raw, recording one global entry; otherwise globals empty. No blob-unload transformation or Schema::validate is performed by this conversion (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:922-927). Descriptor starts immediately after supplied bytes with no alignment repair. Column metadata start follows.

For each page-table column in input order, record current byte position, Any-wrap each Legacy/Structural PageEncoding into Direct, copy all supplied offset/size pairs and preserve num_rows/priority. Collect pages fallibly. No version grammar, bounds, buffer-content or alignment validation and no descriptor relocation; offsets must already be relative to the unchanged data prefix.

Copy column buffer descriptors, Any-wrap column encoding, serialize full ColumnMetadata and append raw bytes, retaining(position,length). Page-table Arc values are borrowed; page/descriptor Vecs and encoded bytes allocate copies. ColumnInfo.index is ignored; output ordering is Vec order.

Append column offset table then global offset table using LEu64 position,length pairs; counts cast unchecked to u32. Return body with original starts and column count page_table.len. No footer, count prefix, checksum or IO here. Mini mode has no global entry and may have coincident global-table/footer start. Extra batch.top_level_columns mapping is unused.

cfg(test) private tests import Arrow/null/schema and EncodingPipeline. analysis helper constructs nullable Boolean child with caller values under parent validity, but declared Lance schema marks changed child nonnullable and analysis parent nullable. Arrow child itself is nullable so fixture can represent invalid visible nulls. It returns ArrayRef and converted Schema; all construction unwraps.

child_nulls_under_a_null_parent_are_writable uses four rows with parent validity true,false,true,false and child true,null,false,null; only calls recursive nullability and unwraps. It proves local hidden-null acceptance in this fixture, not actual file roundtrip or encoder success.

child_nulls_under_a_valid_parent_are_still_rejected makes second parent valid while keeping child null; expect_err then checks message contains changed. It does not assert Error variant or count. Fourth hidden null remains present.

Dictionary test builds Int32 values[10,null], keys[0,1,null], parent validity[true,true,false], actual nullable code child and declared nonnullable code child. Visible key1 logical null must error; row2 physical null is masked. Assert message contains code only, not variant. It exercises helper logical_nulls, no persistence or backend IO.

Sliced-parent test uses four Boolean rows, parent validity true,false,true,true then slices offset1 length3. The first remaining null parent hides child null and helper must succeed. No nested-list, reordered-top-level-batch, spill, abort, overflow, footer or IO test in this module.
